**Write it as.** `leverage Macie integration with Amazon EventBridge` · `monitor, process, and remediate findings`

**Scope.** per finding.

> "You can also leverage Macie integration with Amazon EventBridge and AWS Security Hub CSPM to monitor, process, and remediate findings by using other services, applications, and systems."
> — [What is Amazon Macie?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest/user/what-is-macie.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### macie-results-90-days-export-s3-kms

**Claim.** Macie stores sensitive data discovery results for only 90 days; for long-term storage and retention you configure Macie to encrypt them with an AWS KMS key and store them in an S3 bucket. These repository settings apply only to the current AWS Region (and, for a Macie administrator, only to its own account), so you configure them in each Region where you use Macie.

**Write it as.** `for only 90 days` · `encrypt the results with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key and store them in an S3 bucket`

**Scope.** per AWS account per Region; maximum; not adjustable; without a configured results repository.

> "Macie stores your sensitive data discovery results for only 90 days. To access your results and enable long-term storage and retention of them, configure Macie to encrypt the results with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key and store them in an S3 bucket."
> — [Storing and retaining sensitive data discovery results](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest/user/discovery-results-repository-s3.html)

> "When you configure the settings in Macie, your choices apply only to the current AWS Region. If you're the Macie administrator for an organization, your choices apply only to your account."
> — [Storing and retaining sensitive data discovery results](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest/user/discovery-results-repository-s3.html)

> "If you use Macie in multiple AWS Regions, configure the repository settings for each Region in which you use Macie."
> — [Storing and retaining sensitive data discovery results](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest/user/discovery-results-repository-s3.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### macie-s3-data-estate-scope

**Claim.** Macie works on Amazon S3: it keeps an inventory of your S3 general purpose buckets, evaluates and monitors them for security and access control, and discovers and reports sensitive data stored in Amazon S3.

**Write it as.** `an inventory of your S3 general purpose buckets` · `monitors the buckets for security and access control` · `the data that your organization stores in Amazon S3`

**Scope.** per AWS account per Region.

> "To help you manage the security posture of your organization's Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) data estate, Macie provides you with an inventory of your S3 general purpose buckets, and automatically evaluates and monitors the buckets for security and access control."
> — [What is Amazon Macie?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest/user/what-is-macie.html)

> "Macie also automates discovery and reporting of sensitive data to provide you with a better understanding of the data that your organization stores in Amazon S3."
> — [What is Amazon Macie?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest/user/what-is-macie.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### macie-sra-kms-key-user

**Claim.** If S3 objects are encrypted with a KMS key that you manage, you add the Macie service-linked role as a key user of that key so Macie can scan the data.

**Write it as.** `the Macie service-linked role as a key user`

**Scope.** per KMS key; objects encrypted with a customer managed KMS key.

> "If S3 objects are encrypted with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key that you manage, you can add the Macie service-linked role as a key user to that KMS key to enable Macie to scan the data."
> — [Security OU – Security Tooling account](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/security-reference-architecture/security-tooling.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### macie-sra-move-other-data-to-s3

**Claim.** Macie is optimized for scanning objects in Amazon S3; data from other sources, such as RDS or Aurora snapshot exports or exported DynamoDB tables, can be moved to S3 and then evaluated by Macie.

**Write it as.** `Macie is optimized for scanning objects in Amazon S3.` · `can be moved to Amazon S3 and evaluated by Macie`

**Scope.** per AWS account.

> "Macie is optimized for scanning objects in Amazon S3. As a result, any Macie-supported object type that can be placed in Amazon S3 (permanently or temporarily) can be scanned for sensitive data. This means that data from other sources—for example, periodic snapshot exports of Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) or Amazon Aurora databases, exported Amazon DynamoDB tables, or extracted text files from native or third-party applications—can be moved to Amazon S3 and evaluated by Macie."
> — [Security OU – Security Tooling account](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/security-reference-architecture/security-tooling.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### macie-sra-sensitive-findings-job-creator-only

**Claim.** With Macie managed through AWS Organizations, the delegated administrator can enable or suspend Macie in any account, create discovery jobs for member buckets and view all policy findings, but sensitive data findings can be viewed only by the account that created the sensitive data discovery job.

**Write it as.** `view all policy findings for all member accounts` · `viewed only by the account that created`

**Scope.** per organization.

> "Principals who have the appropriate permissions in the delegated administrator account (in this case, the Security Tooling account) can enable or suspend Macie in any account, create sensitive data discovery jobs for buckets that are owned by member accounts, and view all policy findings for all member accounts. Sensitive data findings can be viewed only by the account that created the sensitive findings job."
> — [Security OU – Security Tooling account](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/security-reference-architecture/security-tooling.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

**Claim.** Macie doesn't analyze S3 objects that use other storage classes, such as S3 Glacier Deep Archive or S3 Express One Zone, and doesn't analyze objects stored in S3 directory buckets; the supported storage classes include S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval, S3 Intelligent-Tiering and S3 One Zone-IA.

**Write it as.** `such as S3 Glacier Deep Archive or S3 Express One Zone` · `Macie doesn't analyze objects that are stored in S3 directory buckets.`

> "Macie doesn’t analyze S3 objects that use other Amazon S3 storage classes, such as S3 Glacier Deep Archive or S3 Express One Zone. In addition, Macie doesn't analyze objects that are stored in S3 directory buckets."
> — [Supported storage classes and formats](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest/user/discovery-supported-storage.html)

> Supported Amazon S3 storage classes: "S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval"
> — [Supported storage classes and formats](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest/user/discovery-supported-storage.html)

> Supported Amazon S3 storage classes: "S3 Intelligent‐Tiering"
> — [Supported storage classes and formats](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest/user/discovery-supported-storage.html)

> Supported Amazon S3 storage classes: "S3 One Zone‐Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone‐IA)"
> — [Supported storage classes and formats](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest/user/discovery-supported-storage.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.
